THE SALT ROAD

by Henry Aldous

Chapter One

The Caravan

The caravan left the city before dawn, forty camels and nine men, and by the time the sun was up the walls were only a brown line on the horizon behind them.

Idris rode at the rear, where the dust was worst, because he was the youngest and because nobody had told him he could ride anywhere else.

On the third night they camped at the dry well. The old drivers called it the Liar, because it had promised water to three generations of travellers and given none.

"Do not drink from it even if it fills," said Rahim. "Especially if it fills."

#

In the morning the well was full to the brim.

Chapter Two

The Liar

Nobody spoke of it at breakfast. The men loaded the camels with their backs to the water, and Rahim counted the animals twice, which he had never done before.

Idris counted too. There were forty-one.
